notes: **Root types:** tap root (dicots, from radicle) and adventitious/fibrous root (monocots, from stem base). Modified roots: tuber, aerial, prop, pneumatophore.
**Stem modifications:** runner, rhizome, corm, tuber, bulb, sucker, stolon, thorn, spine, cladode.
**Leaf types:** simple vs compound, phyllotaxy (alternate, opposite, whorled), venation ( reticulate in dicots, parallel in monocots).
**Inflorescence:** racemose (indeterminate: raceme, spike, panicle, spadix) vs cymose (determinate: monochasial, dichasial).
**Flower parts:** calyx (sepals), corolla (petals), androecium (stamens: filament + anther), gynoecium (carpels: stigma + style + ovary).
**Fruit types:** fleshy (berry, drupe, pome) and dry (dehiscent: legume, follicle, capsule; indehiscent: achene, caryopsis, nut).
**Classification systems:** artificial (Linnaeus, sexual system), natural (Bentham and Hooker, Engler and Prantl), phylogenetic (APG, molecular DNA-based).

**Economic families:** Brassicaceae (mustard, cruciferae, tetradynamous), Fabaceae (legumes, nitrogen fixers, papilionaceous), Solanaceae (potato, tomato, nightshade), Liliaceae (onion, garlic, tulip).
